newsitem.title: INDIA: Infrastructure hampering India GDP growth-Chidambaram.
newsitem.headline: Infrastructure hampering India GDP growth-Chidambaram.

text.p: Indian Finance Minister P.Chidambaram said on Tuesday annual gross domestic product growth could be raised above eight percent if the country's creaking infrastructure is improved.

India's GDP growth was currently running around seven percent annually, Chidamabaram told a gathering of business people and bankers attending a conference on infrastructure development in the wester state of Maharashtra.
"If we can improve infrastructure we can take this up to over eight percent," he told the "Advantage Maharashtra" conference in Bombay by video link from New Delhi.
But the country needs to invest around $130 billion over the next five to seven years in its infrastructure sector.
"The bulk of the money can be raised in India but we also need foreign money, their technology and the new market you can take us to," he told the Indian and foreign audience.
